page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is provisioned with 24 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation. It includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 10.67 GB per vCPU. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, though it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10%, and Geekbench text processing is weak. However, multi-core execution is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average range. Notably, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly, placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the Passmark memory score is weak. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all demonstrate average performance.

The shared CPU allocation presents a tradeoff, as sustained single-core workloads or real-time LLM text generation may experience performance bottlenecks, as evidenced by poor text generation speeds in LLM benchmarks. However, the high memory density of 256.0 GB makes this server a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. This configuration is well-suited for multi-threaded data processing, caching layers, database operations, and memory-heavy web serving applications.
